relatedSnapshot.title: 3. AI Search & Initial State Panel
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Build the main content area's initial state — the "Start your search with AI" panel that appears when the unified lead scraping page first loads (before any filters are applied or search is executed). This panel also includes the search history / saved searches list.

## Layout

This panel occupies the main content area (right of the filter sidebar). It is centered vertically and horizontally within the available space.

### AI Search Card

* Heading: "Start your search with AI"
* Search input field with placeholder text: "E.g Engineers in New York in software companies with more than 500 employees"
* "AI Search" button (sparkle icon + text) to the right of the input
* The AI search input should be a prominent, large input field

### Saved Searches List (below the AI search card)

* Two-column or single list layout showing all saved searches
* Each saved search item shows:
  * Search name/description text
  * Lead count icon with number (e.g. "244k" with people icon)
  * If the search has been partially imported: status badge (e.g. "5k/20k imported" in yellow/amber)
* Clicking a saved search loads its filters into the sidebar and transitions to the results table
* All searches are automatically saved (no separate "recent" vs "saved" — they're the same list)

### Navigation

* "Back" button at bottom-left to go back to lead source selection
* "Next" button at bottom-right (disabled until a search is performed)

## AI Search Behavior

1. User types a natural language prompt (e.g. "Marketing agencies in Name 2 with 10-50 employees")
2. User clicks "AI Search" or presses Enter
3. Loading state shown while AI processes the prompt
4. AI returns structured filter values: job titles, locations, industries, keywords, employee size
5. Name 3 filters are auto-populated with the returned values
6. Sections with values auto-expand in the sidebar
7. The main area transitions from this initial state to the Lead Results Data Table (sub-ticket #4)
8. Lead count is fetched and displayed
9. The search is automatically saved to the saved searches list

## Technical Notes

* The AI search should call an existing or new tRPC mutation that:
  * Takes a natural language string
  * Uses AI (existing niche → filter inference logic from `useLeadCountPreview`) to determine filter values
  * Returns structured `SuperSearchFilters` + job titles + locations + company sizes
* Reuse/extend the existing AI industry inference logic from `use-lead-count-preview.ts`
* Search results persist in state — navigating back to this panel should show updated saved searches list
* Saved searches need a backend data model (see sub-ticket #6 for full saved search implementation)

## Dependencies

* Blocked by: ENG-6029 (Name 1 — needed to display auto-populated filters)

## Priority

P1 — Core user flow; this is the primary entry point for users.

relatedSnapshot.title: Lead search returns non-retail/luxury leads with no preview step
relatedSnapshot.description:
Customer reports that AI and manually filtered lead searches returned \~11k leads that largely do not match the intended ICP (retail / luxury product businesses). Many leads are SaaS or AI agencies despite targeting for retail/luxury.

Current flow adds leads directly into campaigns without a true preview/review step, so mis-targeted leads were imported at scale and used in cold email campaigns. This has resulted in sub-2% positive response rates, no booked calls for about a week, and significant time/credit spend on low-quality/out-of-ICP leads.

Customer feedback:

* Used both AI search (5k leads) and manual filters (6k leads) and still did not get correctly targeted leads
* Wants a way to preview/verify leads before they are added to campaigns
* Requests some form of credit/compensation because the current behavior led to wasted budget and time

relatedSnapshot.title: Dashboard 'Leads Contacted' widget shows 26 because it counts cold-email daily metric rows instead of contacted leads (Company Two)
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Claim: In the workspace "Company Two", the default dashboard "Overview" view shows "Leads Contacted" = 26 while the customer says they have contacted nearly 1,500 leads across their cold email campaigns; the customer also reports the dashboard has looked empty/not synced with the cold email agent for over a week.

Bounded conversation context: Customer (Name 9, workspace "Company Two") opened the conversation asking for a human, saying the dashboard is not updating alongside the cold email agent and that he had already done everything previously suggested. He then specified: "The data from all of the campaigns isn't coming over to the dashboard itself, so it looks empty. For example, we've contacted nearly 1,500 leads, and the dashboard only says we've contacted 26." He gave the workspace name and said it affects all campaigns, not one.

Finding (not an engineering bug): The dashboard is not failing to sync, and the cold email agent data is present. The cause of the "26" is a widget configuration on the workspace's own default dashboard view. The "Leads Contacted" number widget is stored with metric source "Cold Email Agent" and aggregation "Count" and no measure field, so the widget resolves to COUNT(\*) of the cold email daily metrics table. That workspace currently has exactly 26 daily metric rows (4 active campaigns x 7 days of daily analytics, 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-14), which is the 26 the customer sees. The product's own cold email agent dashboard template defines this same tile as Sum of the "New Leads Contacted" measure, not a record count.

Underlying data is healthy:

* 4 active campaigns with 7,670 leads uploaded.
* 1,588 campaign leads have status "contacted"; 39 out-of-office, 33 bounced, 32 replies received, 7 not interested.
* Campaign daily metrics total 1,699 new leads contacted and 2,008 emails sent over 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-14.
* Campaign overview snapshots agree (1,699 contacted unique leads across the four campaigns), i.e. roughly the "nearly 1,500" the customer expects.

Expected behaviour: that widget should be Sum of "New Leads Contacted" (the Cold Email Agent source exposes it as a measure field), which returns about 1,699 for the same "All time" period.

Proposed human action: support walks the workspace owner through editing the widget in the dashboard editor - set Aggregation to Sum and Field to "New Leads Contacted" (or use the built-in "Contacted Leads" metric) - then confirms with the customer that the tile now shows the real count. Worth checking whether other tiles on the same view were built the same way (a widget added on the Cold Email Agent source defaults to Count).

Reopen condition: if the tile is corrected to Sum of New Leads Contacted and still shows a number far below the leads the customer knows were contacted, that would point at the cold email analytics sync rather than the widget and should be re-opened.

relatedSnapshot.title: Set the new lead search filters in the campaign wizard
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-15333: users can set every new lead search filter in the campaign wizard, so they can target by tech stack, hiring and intent signals without the API.

## Problem

The wizard's advanced filters only offer what the builder supported before. Once ENG-15334 ships, API callers can use filters that app users can't see or set.

## User experience

In "Select Your Leads", the advanced filters gain:

* Tech stack and hiring roles, as tag inputs.
* Intent signals: a signal type, "within N days", and optional keywords.
* Exclude locations, and a toggle for matching on the person's location or the company HQ.
* Broad industries (include and exclude) and excluded industries.
* An exact-match toggle next to job titles and excluded titles, and "match any / all" next to keywords.
* The full news, funding stage and seniority lists.

The lead count preview refreshes after each change. The saved campaign shows a chip per filter, a duplicated campaign keeps them, and a section opens automatically when it holds a value.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[New controls] --> F[Campaign form state] --> L[Lead count preview] --> S[Save]
  S --> D[Detail page chips]
  S --> U[Duplicate keeps filters]
```

## What's included

* The controls above, their form fields and defaults, the auto-open sections, the count preview input and save.
* PostHog through the repo's activation tracking skill: the filter step records which advanced filters were used (names only, never the values typed).

## Out of scope

* Filter engine, API and MCP: ENG-15334.
* AI search: ENG-15336.

## Blocked by

ENG-15334

## Done when

* Changing each new control fires a count preview request that carries that filter. How to check: the network log on the PR preview.
* A campaign saved with every new filter shows a chip for each on its detail page, and its duplicate shows the same values in the filter step.
* At 390 px wide, no new control overflows sideways.
* The advanced-filter event lands in PostHog with the filter names.

## Implementation context

* Follow the `acquisity-frontend` rules for the controls. James approves the screenshots before the code review hand-off.

relatedSnapshot.title: Move the AI lead search to GPT-6 Luna and tune it to 80% on-target leads
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-15333: the AI lead search moves to GPT-6 Luna, uses a prompt adapted from Name 17's campaign rules, can propose every new filter, and is tuned against real searches until it returns on-target leads at least 80% of the time. Better AI searches mean better-fit leads and more booked meetings for users who don't build filters by hand.

## Problem

The AI search behind the wizard and the public `ai_search_leads` and `ai_search_campaign_leads` runs two `gemini-2.5-flash` calls. It can only propose titles, keywords, industries, sizes and countries, so it can't use the new filters. It always adds 14 default titles, including Partner, which Name 17 measured pulling in employees. Nobody has measured how often its searches return the right leads.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    B1[Brief] --> G1[Gemini 2.5 Flash x2] --> F1[titles, keywords, industries, sizes, countries]
  end
  subgraph After
    B2[Brief] --> L2[GPT-6 Luna, Gemini fallback] --> F2[+ excludes, tech stack, hiring, signals, news, funding, seniority, match modes, location and industry excludes]
  end
```

Tuning loop (a goal-mode session):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[Prod briefs, last 90 days] --> A[AI search] --> V[Free Company One preview, 25 rows] --> C[Free company lookup] --> J[Jev scores each row] --> S[Accuracy] --> T[Change one thing in the prompt]
  T --> A
```

## What's included

* Both calls move to `openai/gpt-6-luna`, with `gemini-2.5-flash` as fallback. The model that answered is logged on every call.
* A new lead search prompt adapted from Name 17's rules: owner title block, title excludes, simple root keywords, keyword excludes that never drop a sub-niche of the target (anything the brief explicitly targets overrides an inferred exclude, so a brief for outbound agencies never excludes `outbound`), industry bundles by niche, and when to use tech stack, hiring and signals. The shared title and keyword rules other prompts use stay unchanged.
* The output can set every public filter, and a brief's explicit constraint (for example "exclude Canada" or "using HubSpot") is never dropped, including from the suggested wider search.
* A tuning script with a $75 cost cap and a confirm flag. Briefs come from the read-only replica: 3,597 public API AI searches and 3,952 distinct campaign niches. 160 briefs from the last 90 days split into 100 for tuning and 60 held out. Accuracy is the share of preview leads Jev scores as the right kind of company and a decision-maker title. Jev is checked against Claude Opus 5.5 on 100 rows first (at least 85% agreement). Tuning and held-out runs use Luna only. The held-out set stays hidden, with one run per final candidate and at most 2 attempts; a second attempt uses a fresh held-out set with its own baseline run of today's agent. Briefs, per-brief results and sampled leads are customer data, so they stay local; only anonymous aggregates are shared.

## How it should work

* When a brief names no company size, the proposal uses 1-10, 11-20 and 21-50 on every surface, matching what the wizard fills in today. A size in the brief always wins (James, 13 Oct 2026).
* Default titles are settled by the tuning run: today's 14 titles vs Name 17's 7 owner titles, keeping whichever scores higher on the tune set, then confirmed on the held-out set (James, 13 Oct 2026).

## Out of scope

* The campaign agent's own targeting call, which the campaign engine port plan moves onto this prompt later.
* Filter engine and API: ENG-15334. Wizard: ENG-15335.

## Blocked by

ENG-15334. The tuning script and baseline can start before it merges.

## Done when

* On the 60 held-out briefs, mean accuracy is at least 80% and at least 10 points above today's agent measured the same way, with 0 invalid filters, and every brief that names a tool, hiring or signal gets that filter.
* The median lead pool per held-out brief is at least half of the baseline median, so accuracy isn't bought by shrinking pools.
* Name 17 or James scores 50 random held-out rows blind and agrees with Jev on at least 85%. Otherwise the result is inconclusive.
* MCP `ai_search_leads` with "Owners of US marketing agencies using HubSpot, 1-20 staff" proposes `technologies: ["HubSpot"]` and excludes `email` and `outbound` in keywords, and `preview_lead_search` accepts the proposal unchanged.
* With no size in the brief, `ai_search_leads` proposes `companySize: ["1-10", "11-20", "21-50"]`.
* Total tuning spend stays under $75.

## Implementation context

* Name 17's rules come from the campaign engine repo: the targeting knowledge, the keyword filter skill and the expand-TAM playbook.
* A direct check on 13 Oct 2026 showed Luna on OpenRouter accepts our strict schema with `minItems: 3` and `temperature: 0`.
* Related: ENG-12682 (bare title tokens) and ENG-14916 (save resolved titles on AI searches).

relatedSnapshot.title: Search Leads with Manual Filters
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let external applications find and add leads using exact caller-supplied filters without asking AI to invent the targeting.

## Context

Manual filters and AI lead search should use one provider-neutral Acquisity filter model. A caller that already knows the required targeting should be able to validate, preview, edit and execute it directly.

The API must execute the supplied filters without silently broadening them.

## Scope

* Define the canonical Acquisity lead-search filter schema.
* Add a filter-options endpoint with stable IDs, labels and validation constraints.
* Support job titles, seniority, departments, industries, locations, company size, revenue, keywords, company names, domains, funding/news signals and lookalikes where currently supported.
* Create a versioned manual lead-search plan bound to one draft campaign or build.
* Validate filters and return warnings for missing targeting dimensions without blocking structurally valid filters.
* Preview the available lead count before paid execution.
* Allow edits before execution using version checks.
* Treat the caller's manual filter document as explicit approval for that exact version.
* Execute the plan once, attach winning leads to the draft campaign and deduplicate them against other campaign sources.
* Preserve hard filters exactly during execution.
* Return Acquisity counts, warnings and errors only.
* Add filter validation, versioning, single-execution, billing and tenant-boundary tests.

## Dependencies and parallel work

* **Blocked by:** Create draft campaign (ENG-12015) and Add shared idempotency and operation polling (ENG-12014).
* **Can run in parallel with:** Create sequence and Import leads through one ingestion pipeline.
* **Blocks:** Search Leads with AI and Build Complete Campaigns.

## Acceptance criteria

* A caller can construct valid filters using the documented option catalogue.
* Previewing does not execute or bill for the search.
* Execution uses the exact approved filter version.
* Filters are never silently broadened.
* A plan cannot be edited or executed a second time after execution starts.
* Matching leads are attached once to the intended draft campaign.
* Public payloads contain no internal search-provider fields.

## PR size

Target **1,200–1,800 changed lines**, including migrations and tests. Split before implementation if the estimate reaches 2,000 lines.

## Definition of Done

This ticket must satisfy all eight Definition of Done items on ENG-12011, including scope registration, its reference page shipping in the same PR, the provider-term gate, use of the shared idempotency and operation-polling mechanism, a conformance entry, token-derived audit actor, the size cap, and the cold-start check by both implementer and tester.

relatedSnapshot.title: Public API: standalone lead search (preview + AI filters, then paid search + export)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Summary

Add a **standalone lead-discovery surface** to the public API under `/v1/workspaces/{id}/leads`, distinct from campaign-leads: run a provider (Company One SuperSearch) search from a filter document — manually or from an AI-generated brief — and export the matching leads for use **outside** the platform (not attached to a campaign).

## Design

Reuses the campaign search's filter contract, count service, and AI generator; the export is a **separate, user-triggered step** (not baked into the search operation):

1. `POST /leads/search/preview` — count + redacted sample (no emails). Free.
2. `POST /leads/search/ai` — brief → canonical filter document + estimate. Free.
3. `POST /leads/search` (paid) — run a campaign-less scrape → leads land in a `lead_scrape_run` → fire `lead_search.completed` webhook ("your leads are ready", carries `searchId`). Bills the **actual** scraped count. *(next phase)*
4. `GET /leads/search/{searchId}/export` — the **consumer triggers the download**; reuses the existing `exportCampaignLeads` CSV machinery over the scrape run's leads. *(next phase)*

## Shipped in this PR — free tier

* New `leads` public-API permission resource (`read`).
* `POST /leads/search/preview` + `POST /leads/search/ai` (functional).
* Extended `countSuperSearchLeads` to surface the provider's redacted sample (non-breaking).
* `Leads` OpenAPI tag; `leads.preview` / `leads.ai_search` handlers.

## Next phase — paid search + separate export

* Re-add `leads:search` scope; `POST /leads/search` route + handler (campaign-less scrape dispatch via `ai-clients/apify-lead-generator.created`, no `campaignId`).
* New gated `lead-export.scrape-completed` event in `process-lead-scrape.ts`; `leads.search` handler waits on it → debits actual count → emits `lead_search.completed` webhook (trigger-catalog + outbound-events entries).
* `GET /leads/search/{searchId}/export` reusing the CSV/export machinery.
* Docs guide + tests.

Merged `origin/main` to pick up the ENG-13106 outbound-webhook system, which the paid path builds on.

relatedSnapshot.title: 6. Saved Searches Modal & Auto-Save Backend
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Build the saved searches system including: the saved searches modal UI, auto-save behavior for every search, rename/delete functionality, and the backend data model to persist searches.

## Saved Searches Modal

Triggered by clicking the "Saved Searches" button in the results table top bar.

### Modal Layout

* **Header**: "Search..." title with close (X) button
* **Search/Rename Input**: Text input at top for searching through saved searches or renaming the currently selected search. Has checkmark (save) and X (cancel) action buttons.
* **Saved Searches List**: Scrollable list of all saved searches, each showing:
  * Search name/description text (auto-generated from filter values, e.g. "United States, Software & Name 19, CEO, owner, business...")
  * Lead count with people icon (e.g. "244k")
  * If search is currently being scraped/imported: status badge showing progress (e.g. "5k/20k imported" in yellow/amber badge with refresh icon)
* **Hover State**: On hover, each list item reveals:
  * Edit (pencil) icon — enters rename mode for that search
  * Delete (trash) icon — deletes the saved search (with confirmation)
* **Click Behavior**: Clicking a saved search item loads its filters into the sidebar, transitions to results table, and fetches updated lead count

## Auto-Save Behavior

* Every search (AI or manual filter application) is automatically saved
* Auto-generated name based on applied filters (e.g. comma-separated summary of key filters)
* Users can rename saved searches via the modal
* Saved searches persist across sessions (stored in database)

## "Save Search" Button (in top bar)

* Clicking "Save Search" in the results table top bar saves the current filter state
* If the current search already exists (was loaded from saved searches), it updates the existing saved search
* Shows a brief success toast/notification

## Backend Data Model

New database table/model needed:

```
saved_lead_searches:
  - id (UUID, primary key)
  - organization_id (FK to organizations)
  - user_id (FK to users, who created it)
  - name (string — auto-generated or user-renamed)
  - filters (JSONB — stores the complete filter state: job titles, locations, industries, keywords, employee sizes, advanced filters, etc.)
  - ai_prompt (string, nullable — the original AI search prompt if applicable)
  - lead_count (integer, nullable — cached lead count at time of save)
  - import_status (enum: null | 'importing' | 'partial' | 'complete')
  - imported_count (integer, default 0)
  - total_to_import (integer, nullable)
  - created_at (timestamp)
  - updated_at (timestamp)
```

## tRPC Name 18

* `savedSearches.list` — list all saved searches for the current organization
* `savedSearches.create` — create a new saved search
* `savedSearches.update` — update name or filters of a saved search
* `savedSearches.delete` — delete a saved search
* `savedSearches.getById` — load a specific saved search with its filters

## Technical Notes

* Use Drizzle ORM for the database schema (follow repo conventions)
* Generate migrations with `bun db:generate` (never hand-write migrations)
* The saved searches list in the AI Search initial state panel (ENG-6030) should use the same `savedSearches.list` endpoint
* Consider optimistic updates for rename/delete operations
* Use `ds-*` design system variables for modal styling

## Dependencies

* Blocked by: ENG-6031 (Lead Results Data Table — the modal is triggered from the table's top bar)
* Also connects to: ENG-6030 (AI Search Panel uses the same saved searches list)

## Priority

P2 — Important for user workflow but the core search/filter/table flow can work without saved searches initially.

relatedSnapshot.title: Lead search: every Company One filter, plus a tuned GPT-6 Luna AI search
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let users, API callers and the AI lead search target leads by everything Company One's lead search offers, so campaigns can aim at buying triggers like tech stack, hiring and intent signals and book more meetings. Today we send 8 fewer filters than Company One accepts and only part of 6 more, because our filter builder was written before Company One added them. This master adds the missing filters to the filter engine, the public API and MCP, the campaign wizard, and the AI lead search, which also moves to GPT-6 Luna with a prompt tuned on real searches.

## Problem

Every lead search, whether it starts in the wizard, the public API, MCP or the AI search, becomes one filter document that our builder turns into Company One's `search_filters`. The builder only knows the filters that existed when it was written. Comparing Company One's live count-leads API spec (13 Oct 2026) with our builder on `main` shows these gaps:

| Company One filter | What users get | Today |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `technologies` | Companies using a tool, such as HubSpot | Missing |
| `jobListing` | Companies hiring for a role | Missing |
| `signals` | Job changes, traffic surges, LinkedIn activity in the last N days | Missing |
| `locations.exclude` | Exclude places | Missing |
| `location_mode` | Match on the company's HQ instead of the person | Missing |
| `industry` (19 broad groups) | Broad industry, include and exclude | Missing |
| `subIndustry.exclude` | Exclude industries | Include only |
| `title.includeMode` / `excludeMode` | Exact job title match | Contains only |
| `keyword_filter.include_mode` | Require all keywords | Any only |
| `news`, `funding_type`, `level` | Full lists of 28, 23 and 18 values | 10, 10 and 11 values |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W[Wizard] --> D[Public filter document]
  A[Public API and MCP] --> D
  AI[AI lead search] --> D
  D --> B[SuperSearch filter builder]
  B --> I[Company One count, preview, search]
  classDef child1 fill:#d6f5e3,stroke:#1a7f4b
  classDef child2 fill:#dbe9ff,stroke:#2457a6
  classDef child3 fill:#fff1cc,stroke:#a66b00
  class D,B,A child1
  class W child2
  class AI child3
```

Green is child 1 (filter engine, API and MCP), blue is child 2 (wizard) and yellow is child 3 (AI lead search).

## User experience

In the campaign wizard, users can pick tech stack, hiring roles, intent signals with a "within N days" window, excluded places, company HQ location matching, broad industries, excluded industries, exact title matching and "match all keywords", plus the full news, funding and seniority lists. API and MCP callers get the same filters with the same names. The AI search proposes these filters when a brief asks for them, for example "agencies using HubSpot" or "companies hiring SDRs".

## What's included

1. The filter engine, public API and MCP accept and send every new filter, with docs and the published spec updated. Existing searches send exactly what they send today.
2. The campaign wizard shows the new filters, the lead count updates, saved and duplicated campaigns keep them, and PostHog records which advanced filters people use.
3. The AI lead search runs on GPT-6 Luna with a prompt adapted from Name 17's campaign rules, can propose every new filter, and is tuned in a goal-mode run against real prod briefs until Jev scores at least 80% of returned leads as on-target.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets explicitly grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they still keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none.

1. ENG-15334: every new filter through the filter engine, public API and MCP.

### Wave 2: starts when ENG-15334 merges

Parallel: ENG-15335 and ENG-15336.

2. ENG-15336: blocked by ENG-15334.
3. ENG-15335: blocked by ENG-15334.

Cross-wave overlap:

* ENG-15336's tuning script and baseline run may start while ENG-15334 is underway, because they measure today's agent; proposing the new filters waits for the merge.

## Out of scope

* Company One company lists and website visitors (James, 13 Oct 2026).
* Custom company sizes and max leads per company: owned by the campaign engine API master, in its company-size and max-per-company children.
* The campaign agent's own targeting call, which the campaign engine port plan will move onto this prompt later.
* Lead providers other than Company One. They ignore the new filters; a local business search rejects them like other B2B-only filters.

## Name 20 and rollback

Every new filter is optional, so nothing changes for a search that doesn't use one. Roll back in reverse order (child 3, then 2, then 1), because children 2 and 3 produce filters only child 1 accepts. Child 1 isn't reverted while stored campaigns carry a new filter, because the old code would drop it and re-scrape more broadly than the user asked; roll forward instead. Child 3's model and prompt change ships behind its tuning result.

## Decisions made

* **Default company size (James, 13 Oct 2026):** when a brief names no size, the AI search proposes 1-50 employees (1-10, 11-20, 21-50) on every surface. The wizard already fills this in today; the public API and MCP AI search set no size, so child 3 makes them match.
* **Default titles (James, 13 Oct 2026):** the tuning run decides between today's 14 titles and Name 17's 7 owner titles (Partner and Principal only for law, consulting and accounting), keeping whichever Jev scores higher on the tune set.

## How we'll measure

AI search accuracy: the share of preview leads Jev scores as the right kind of company with a decision-maker title, averaged over 60 held-out prod briefs from the last 90 days. Today's value is measured as the baseline at the start of child 3. Target: 80% or more, and at least 10 points above the baseline. Read when child 3's tuning run finishes.

## Done when

* A lead search from any surface can use every filter in the table above, and Company One receives it.
* A search that uses none of the new filters sends the same request to Company One as before.
* The AI search meets the accuracy target on the held-out briefs, and a human spot check agrees with Jev on at least 85% of 50 rows.

## Implementation context

* Company One count-leads API reference: developer.Company One.ai
* Related: ENG-11163 (US text location ignored by Company One). A free preview on 13 Oct 2026 returned 50 of 50 US leads for a text "United States" location, so it looks fixed on Company One's side.
* Related: ENG-12682 (AI lead search bare title tokens), which child 3's title rules address.

relatedSnapshot.title: Search Leads with AI
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Turn a natural-language targeting brief into an editable lead-search plan that can be reviewed before leads are purchased or attached.

## Context

AI lead search is not a separate lead system. It produces the same canonical Acquisity filter document used by manual search.

AI must preserve explicit hard constraints and must never silently broaden a low-volume search.

## Scope

* Add AI search mode with a natural-language brief, requested lead count and optional hard constraints.
* Build generation context from the caller-supplied campaign context and targeting brief.
* Generate the same canonical filter document used by manual search.
* Return the proposed filters, assumptions, warnings, rationale and estimated available count.
* Store suggested expansion separately from the exact proposal.
* Default to review and approval before paid execution.
* Allow automatic approval only when explicitly requested by a key with the paid-execution scope.
* Preserve hard constraints during generation, editing and execution.
* Block zero-result execution and return actionable suggestions.
* Reuse the manual plan's versioning, preview, execution, deduplication and attachment flow.
* Use existing lead-credit and capacity checks with retry-safe billing references.
* Keep model and internal provider names out of public responses.
* Add focused prompt evaluations plus approval, hard-constraint and billing tests.

## Dependencies and parallel work

* **Blocked by:** Search Leads with Manual Filters.
* **Can run in parallel with:** Generate Sequences with AI, and the lifecycle tickets once their own prerequisites are complete.
* **Blocks:** Build Complete Campaigns.

## Acceptance criteria

* A natural-language brief produces an editable canonical filter plan.
* The caller can see what the AI assumed before execution.
* Hard constraints are never removed or weakened.
* Low-volume searches suggest changes rather than applying them automatically.
* Paid execution requires the correct scope and exact approved version.
* The resulting leads use the same attachment and deduplication path as manual search.
* Public responses expose no AI model or outreach-provider details.

## PR size

Target **1,000–1,500 changed lines**, including evaluations and tests. Split before implementation if the estimate reaches 2,000 lines.

## Definition of Done

This ticket must satisfy all eight Definition of Done items on ENG-12011, including scope registration, its reference page shipping in the same PR, the provider-term gate, use of the shared idempotency and operation-polling mechanism, a conformance entry, token-derived audit actor, the size cap, and the cold-start check by both implementer and tester.

relatedSnapshot.title: "Add connection" tab should have search option
relatedSnapshot.description:
<image> 

## Problem

In the **Add connection** tab, integrations can currently be found by typing, but the search interaction is fragile. If the input contains a typo, the current interaction requires closing the modal and opening it again to recover and continue searching.

This makes finding an integration unnecessarily error-prone and slows down connection setup.

## Solution

Add a visible search field to the **Add connection** tab so integrations can be filtered directly and the query can be edited in place without resetting the modal.

Search behavior should follow the same idea used inside the workflow creator.

## Scope

* Add a search input to the integration selection UI in the **Add connection** modal.
* Allow users to type, edit, and clear the query without closing the modal.
* Filter the visible integration list based on the current query.
* Keep the rest of the connection creation flow unchanged.

## UX behavior

* The search field is available when the integration list is open.
* Keyboard focus moves to the search field automatically when the modal opens.
* Typing filters the list of integrations using the same search behavior as the workflow creator.
* Matching is case-insensitive, so queries like `airtable` match `Airtable`.
* Filtering supports partial matches, not only prefix matches.
* Users can correct typos by editing the query directly.
* Clearing the query restores the full integration list.
* Search results are fully filtered by the current query rather than keeping commonly used integrations pinned above the filtered results.
* The modal remains open while searching and editing the query.

## Acceptance criteria

* A search field is present in the **Add connection** tab.
* Keyboard focus is placed in the search field when the modal opens.
* Entering text filters the integration list using the same behavior as the workflow creator.
* Editing a previously entered query updates results without closing and reopening the modal.
* Clearing the query resets the list to all available integrations.
* Filtered results do not keep pinned or unfiltered integrations above the matches.
* A typo in the query does not force the user to restart the flow.

## Open questions or design follow-ups

* Confirm whether the workflow creator search implementation can be reused directly here, or whether this modal needs a separate implementation with matching behavior.

## Outcome

Users can find and correct integration searches inside the modal without having to close and reopen the flow.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make People search find a lead in under half a second
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-14952, and the first ticket to pick up. Make a rep's search on the People tab find a lead in under half a second on every workspace, so reps spend calls selling, not waiting. Sales reps on the AI Acquisition Sales Team report that finding a call lead in People "takes a minute or more and doesn't load", and they search contacts all day.

## Problem

What we saw on 8 Oct 2026, as a user on the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace (159,158 contacts), from the in-app browser:

* Every search takes 2.5 to 3 s before rows show, even for one exact name. Each pause in typing sends two searches (rows and count), and nothing cancels the old ones, so a rep typing a name stacks up slow searches on the database. PlanetScale shows contact search at 2.2 s at the median and 12 s at the 99th percentile, with a 30 s timeout. That's where "a minute" comes from when searches pile up.
* **A formatted phone number finds nothing.** "<phone>" returns "No matching people", while "4407598888" finds the contact. Reps copy numbers in this format from calls, so they think search is broken.
* Opening the record and the note box takes about 0.4 s, so the slow part is search, not the record.

The cause: ENG-14533 built a fast search index, but the job that builds it has never reached this workspace. It builds 3 workspaces every 15 minutes in no useful order, across 10,275 workspaces of which only 2,928 have contacts, and the biggest workspace it has built has 6,111 contacts. So this workspace still runs the old search, which scans every contact, email and address for each keystroke pause.

## How it works

Today:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Rep pauses typing] --> B[Rows search and count search]
  B --> C[No index: scan 159k contacts]
  C --> D[2.5 s to 30 s, old searches keep running]
```

After this change:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Rep pauses typing] --> B["CHANGED: cancel the old search"]
  B --> C["CHANGED: index finds matching ids"]
  C --> D[Rows show, count follows]
```

## What's included

* **Build the index for the biggest workspaces now.** Build the AI Acquisition Sales Team and Name 23 indexes straight away, after timing one build on a mid-size workspace. Then make the job build first-time indexes largest first, by contacts, companies and deals, and skip workspaces with none. Keep repairs on their own fair turn, and retry a failed build without blocking the queue.
* **Phone and email fast paths.** A search that's mostly digits matches phone numbers by their digits, whatever the formatting, in both the People search and the note and task record picker. A search with an  at  matches emails directly.
* **Let the index drive the search.** Today the indexed search is an OR of several sub-searches (index, notes, owner name, custom fields), which may stop the index being used. Check it with EXPLAIN on the read replica on this workspace once the index exists, and rewrite it as one list of candidate ids if it does.
* **Stop stacking searches.** Cancel a search when the rep keeps typing, and stop it on the server too. Run the count only after the rows have come back.
* **The note and task record picker.** "Add call notes" lets reps pick a person, and that picker uses its own old search. Move it onto the same index.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none.

1. Build the fast search index for the biggest workspaces first: on-demand build, largest first, empty workspaces skipped, repairs on their own share; then build the two largest workspaces.

### Wave 2: starts once the index is built on the largest workspaces

Parallel: none.

2. People search and the note picker find a lead fast, including by a formatted phone number: blocked by Build the fast search index for the biggest workspaces first.

Cross-wave overlap: none verified. The search work needs EXPLAIN against a real index on a large workspace.

## Out of scope

The sample-data wait on list pages is ENG-14953.

## Done when

* The AI Acquisition Sales Team, Name 23 and every workspace with over 5,000 contacts have a ready index. How to check: a read-only query on the index state table.
* On the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace, People search shows rows in under 0.5 s at p90 for names, emails and phone numbers. How to check: Axiom over 7 days after release, and the browser's network timing.
* "<phone>", "<phone>" and "4407598888" all find the same contact, in People search and in the note picker.
* Typing a name quickly leaves at most one search running per list on the server.

## Implementation context

* Rebuild job: `lib/inngest/functions/crm/rebuild-record-search-index-cron.ts` (3 workspaces per run, every 15 minutes) and the selection in record-search-index-maintenance.ts. There's no way to build one workspace on demand today.
* Search: record-search.ts; the list procedure in `trpc/routers/crm/contact.ts` (search near line 650, count near line 739); debounce 300 ms in `crm-list-screen.tsx`; `abortOnUnmount` is off.
* Phone digits: a digits trigram index already exists on `crm_telephone` and isn't used by search.
* Note picker: `crm.entities.searchCrmEntities` in `trpc/routers/crm/entities.ts` (near lines 260 to 311).
* Risk: each build batch is 2,000 records under a 30 s statement timeout, and nobody has timed a build over 6,111 contacts. Time a mid-size workspace first, and run the biggest builds watching database load.
* Evidence and timings: the master's AI context.md, and the browser timings recorded on 8 Oct 2026.

relatedSnapshot.title: Return campaign lead search totals from the paged query
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Refined implementation brief

*Refined on 2026-07-20. This is the current delivery brief.*

### Outcome

Return exact campaign-lead search totals from the paged search query so the application does not evaluate the same large search predicate twice.

### Scope

* Add `count(*) over()` to the existing paged campaign-lead query.
* Use the window total for non-empty pages and remove the normal separate count query.
* Return zero for an empty first page.
* Use a bounded fallback or pagination-clamping path for an empty later page.
* Preserve global search, advanced filters, sorting, tenant boundaries, campaign boundaries, and soft-delete filtering.
* Exclude trigram indexes, generated search columns, metadata denormalization, and a new full-text subsystem.

### Acceptance criteria

* Non-empty search and advanced-filter pages execute the expensive predicate once.
* Totals retain parity across global search, field filters, combined filters, and unfiltered pagination.
* Empty first-page and later-page behavior is deterministic.
* Other organizations, campaigns, and soft-deleted rows cannot affect totals.
* The API and UI retain their pagination contract.

### Implementation direction

Return a window total with each selected lead row. Use it as the normal exact total and reserve a bounded secondary path only for an empty non-first page. Rebase after ENG-11249 and PR #5463 if necessary.

### Validation

* Add focused repository and router tests for total parity and empty-page behavior.
* Confirm the standalone count fingerprint disappears after deployment.
* Compare remaining paged-query latency and CPU with the prior paired fingerprints.
* Revisit index work only if the remaining single query is still material.

## Original description

## Summary

**#14 by total DB runtime (1.01%)** over the last 24h, and one of the **slowest per-call queries in the workload**: p50 **3.95s**, p99 **23.5s**, max **23.5s** across 97 calls, reading **634.9k rows/call (\~6,545 rows/query)**. It is the `count(*)` companion to the campaign-lead advanced-search list — a `LEFT JOIN outreach_campaign_lead → lead_scrape_lead` with a large `OR` of leading-wildcard `ILIKE` predicates across many text columns **and** ~20 JSONB `metadata` paths. Filter builder source: `apps/web/lib/outreach/db/campaign.ts` (per-field ILIKE / JSONB `metadata::jsonb -> ... ->> ...` conditions, e.g. `linkedinUrl` block ~L13307).

## Query (normalized, abbreviated)

```sql
SELECT count(*)
FROM outreach_campaign_lead
LEFT JOIN lead_scrape_lead
  ON outreach_campaign_lead.internal_lead_id = lead_scrape_lead.id
WHERE outreach_campaign_lead.campaign_id = $1
  AND outreach_campaign_lead.organization_id = $2
  AND (
    outreach_campaign_lead.email      ILIKE $3
    OR outreach_campaign_lead.full_name  ILIKE $4
    OR outreach_campaign_lead.first_name ILIKE $5
    OR outreach_campaign_lead.last_name  ILIKE $6
    OR lead_scrape_lead.title      ILIKE $7
    OR lead_scrape_lead.company    ILIKE $8
    OR lead_scrape_lead.linkedin_url ILIKE $9
    OR lead_scrape_lead.state      ILIKE $10
    OR lead_scrape_lead.country    ILIKE $11
    OR outreach_campaign_lead.metadata::jsonb -> ... ->> ... ILIKE $..  -- ~20 JSONB paths
  )
```

## Metrics (last 24h, PlanetScale Insights)

| Metric | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Total time | 575k ms (1.01% of DB runtime) |
| Calls | 97 |
| p50 / p99 / max | **3.95s / 23.5s / 23.5s** |
| rows read | 634.9k (~6,545/query) |
| egress | tiny (count only) |

Index usage: `outreach_campaign_lead_campaign_org_lower_email_idx` (100%) and `lead_scrape_lead_pkey` (100%) — the index narrows to the campaign+org slice, but the `OR ... ILIKE` block then forces a **scan of the whole campaign's leads** (and their joined scrape rows) applying leading-wildcard `ILIKE` and JSONB extraction to each row. Large campaigns → ~6.5k rows scanned per call, seconds of CPU.

## Root cause

* **Leading-wildcard** `ILIKE` **on many columns cannot use a b-tree index**; every lead in the campaign is examined.
* The **JSONB** `metadata` **extractions** (~20 paths, `->` / `->>`) run per row, compounding cost.
* Joining `lead_scrape_lead` just to search its text columns widens each scanned row.
* The `count(*)` runs the full predicate over the whole matching set (no `LIMIT`), so it is strictly more expensive than the paged list it accompanies.

## Recommended fix

1. **Full-text / trigram index**: add a `pg_trgm` GIN index on the searched text columns (`email`, `full_name`, `first_name`, `last_name` on `outreach_campaign_lead`; `title`, `company`, `linkedin_url` on `lead_scrape_lead`) so `ILIKE '%term%'` can use an index, or maintain a combined `tsvector` search column.
2. **Name 24 the searched JSONB metadata** into real columns (or a generated column) so the ~20 `metadata` ILIKE paths become indexable instead of per-row extraction.
3. **Avoid recomputing the count** on every keystroke — debounce, cache the count per (campaign, search) for a short TTL, or use an estimated count for large result sets and only compute exact counts on demand.
4. Consider restricting which fields participate in the default "global" search to reduce the OR fan-out.

*Filed by the daily PlanetScale performance review automation. Metrics are 24h aggregates as of 2026-07-11.*
